chunks: Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Imran al-Daqqaq (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Abi al-Kufi narrated to us, saying: Jarir ibn Hazim narrated to me from Abu Masruq, saying:

A group of the Waqifites entered upon Ar-Rida (peace be upon him), among them were Ali ibn Abi Hamza al-Bata'i, Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Ammar, Al-Husayn ibn Imran, and Al-Husayn ibn Abi Sa'id al-Mukari. Ali ibn Abi Hamza said to him, 'May I be your ransom, inform us about your father (peace be upon him), what is his condition?' He said, 'He has passed away (peace be upon him).' He said to him, 'To whom did he entrust (the Imamate)?' He said, 'To me.' He said to him, 'You are saying something that none of your forefathers, Ali ibn Abi Talib and those below him, have said.' He said, 'But the best of my forefathers and the most excellent of them, the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family), has said it.' He said to him, 'Do you not fear these (the Abbasids) for yourself?' He said, 'If I feared them, I would be assisting them against me. The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) was visited by Abu Lahab who threatened him. The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said to him, 'If I am scratched by you with a scratch, then I am a liar.' This was the first verse that the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) derived from it, and it is the first verse I derive for you: 'If I am scratched with a scratch from Harun, then I am a liar.'

Al-Husayn ibn Mihran said to him, 'We have obtained what we seek if you make this statement public.' He said, 'What do you want? Do I want to go to Harun and say to him, 'I am the Imam and you are nothing'? No, this is not what the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) did at the beginning of his mission. He only said this to his family, his clients, and those who trusted him, and he singled them out with it among the people. And you believe the Imamate for those who were before me from my forefathers, and you say that what prevents Ali ibn Musa from informing that his father is alive is Taqiyyah (concealment). So I do not practice Taqiyyah with you in saying that I am the Imam, so how should I practice Taqiyyah with you in claiming that he is alive if he were alive?'

The compiler of this book (may God have mercy on him) said, 'The reason he did not fear Ar-Rashid was because there was a covenant with him that his companion (Al-Ma'mun) was below him (in authority/lineage).'

key_terms.أَبُو لَهَبٍ: Abu Lahab, the uncle of the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.)
key_terms.التَّقِيَّة: Taqiyyah, the practice of concealing one's faith or beliefs to avoid harm
key_terms.الرِّضَا: Ar-Rida, the title of Imam Ali ibn Musa (a.s.)
key_terms.الوَاقِفَةِ: The Waqifites, a Shia sect who believed Imam Ali ibn Musa (a.s.) died and did not accept his son as successor
key_terms.هَارُونَ: Harun, referring to Harun al-Rashid, the Abbasid Caliph

ai.seo_question: Why did Imam Ar-Rida (a.s.) not publicly announce his Imamate like his forefathers?
ai.summary: Imam Ar-Rida (a.s.) refutes the Waqifites' claim that Imam Ali al-Rida (a.s.) should have publicly declared his father's survival by citing the Prophet’s strategic concealment of his status from the general public, reserving it for his trusted inner circle. He argues that if Imam Ali ibn Musa (a.s.) remained silent due to Taqiyyah, Imam Ar-Rida’s own public declaration of the Imamate proves he is not bound by the same concealment, thereby validating the continuity of leadership. This dialogue highlights the Shia scholarly distinction between the necessity of Taqiyyah in times of political danger and the clarity of Imamate when the Imam is secure.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 47-20 Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Imran ad-Daqqaq - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Muhammad ibn Abi Abdullah al-Kufi quoted on the authority of Jareer ibn Hazim, on the authority of Abi Masrooq,

“A group of the waqafites went to see Ar-Ridha’ (a.s.). Ali ibn Hamza al-Bata’ini, Ibn Ishaq ibn Ammar, Al-Husayn ibn Mihran, Al-Hassan ibn Abi Sa’eed al-Mokari were amongst them. Ali ibn Hamza asked the Imam (a.s.), ‘May I be your ransom! What do you know about your father? How is his health?’ The Imam (a.s.) said, ‘In fact, he (a.s.) has died.’ Ali ibn Hamza asked, ‘Who has your father (a.s.) introduced to succeed him?’ The Imam (a.s.) replied, ‘Me.’ Ali ibn Hamza said, ‘You aresaying what none of your forefathers starting with Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) and those who came after him have said.’ The Imam (a.s.) said, ‘But the best and the noblest of my forefathers who is the Prophet of God (a.s.) has said that.’ Ali ibn Hamza said, ‘Don’t you feel threatened by this tribe (the Abbasids) and aren’t you afraid of them?’ The Imam (a.s.) said, ‘If I fear them, I have assisted them against me. Abu Lahab went to the Prophet of God (a.s.) and threatened him. God’s Prophet (S) told him, ‘If I should fear you in the least, I have lied. I have lied about my Prophethood.’ This was the first sign of the Prophet of God (a.s.). This is also my first sign for you. I have lied if Harun harms me in the least.’

Al-Husayn ibn Mihran said, ‘You have done what we want when you publicly announce your Divine Leadership.’ The Imam (a.s.) asked that man, ‘Do you want me to go to Harun in person and tell him that I am the do this in the beginning of his call. The Prophet (S) only Divine Leader and he is nothing? The Prophet of God (a.s.) did not inform his near relatives, friends and trusted friends about his Prophethood, and invited them to accept Islam. The Prophet (S) did not invite all the people. You have accepted the Divine Leadership of my forefathers and think that Ali ibn Musa (a.s.) is denying his father being alive due to the concealment of faith. But how is it that I announce my Divine Leadership to you without any concealment of faith, and openly declare that I am the Divine Leader? If my father (a.s.) was alive, how could I hide it from you and tell you that he (a.s.) has passed away?’”

The author of this book (a.s.heikh Sadooq) - may God have Mercy upon him - said, “The reason why the Imam (a.s.) did not fear (Harun) Ar-Rashid was due to the Covenant he had in which his murderer was declared to be Al-Ma’mun and no one else.”
